Elden Ring

Boss: Erdtree Burial Watchdogs

Edit Page

This boss is encountered in multiple locations throughout the Lands Between, however, their attack movesets may differ based on the weapon they wield.

The Erdtree Burial Watchdogs are located in the following areas:

  • Stormfoot Catacombs in Limgrave, West
    • Reward: 1300 Runes and the Noble Sorcerer Ashes
  • Impaler's Catacombs in the Weeping Peninsula
    • Reward: 2400 Runes and the Demi-Human Ashes
  • Cliffbottom Catacombs in Liurnia of the Lakes, East
    • Reward: 3200 Runes and the Kaiden Sellsword Ashes
  • Minor Erdtree Catacombs in Caelid
    • Reward: 7400 Runes and the Mad Pumpkin Head Ashes
  • Wyndham Catacombs in the Altus Plateau
    • Reward: 12000 Runes and the Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [1]


Sword

The Erdtree Burial Watchdog isn't a "dog" at all. This mummified Egyptian burial cat moves rather mechanically, making its attacks pretty easy to identify, but don't be fooled into a false sense of security.

While the Erdtree Burial Watchdog doesn't have standard movement, it can easily close the distance through attacks. If it stands up, it'll slowly walk toward you before slashing downward. On the other hand, if it grips its sword in both hands and raises it into the air, it'll perform a plunging attack that damages nearby enemies.

Melee characters can easily avoid most of the Erdtree Burial Watchdog's attacks with a well-timed roll to the side, where they can usually get in a few attacks, but don't get greedy, as the boss will often counter with a sweeping slash or 360-degree spin. Alternatively, attacking it from behind will result in the boss turning its head around - exorcist-style - before smashing its flaming tail on the ground.

Since nowhere is safe for long, close-quarters fighters will need to move in to attack during the Erdtree Burial Watchdog's recovery periods and then back away to predict its next attack. While keeping your distance, watch out for the boss' lunging thrust attack, as well as a flaming breath attack, since the flames reach a considerable distance and the boss will rotate to track you.

As for ranged combat, this fight is considerably easier since you simply need to keep your distance. This means watching out for the two attacks initially mentioned, as well as the lunging thrust.
Note that there is also a three-headed variant of this boss, as well as a variant that uses lightning attacks rather than fire, however, they are not significantly different from the default version.


Scepter

Unlike the previous encounters with the Erdtree Burial Watchdog, which wielded a sword, this variant of the boss wields a scepter that grants it some new attacks.

Despite being nearly identical to the three-headed version of the sword-wielding Erdtree Burial Watchdog, its scepter does grant it some magical abilities. In particular, the previously mentioned plunging attack now has a wider range and is imbued with magic, however, its ability to use the Sorcery of the Crozier skill is the biggest change to its arsenal. This attack, used primarily when at range, creates a ring of glintstone projectiles around the boss that then hone in on a target.

While these changes to the Erdtree Burial Watchdog's aren't significant, you'll want to be able to identify them. Use similar tactics to the previous encounters, adjusting as needed, and you shouldn't have too much trouble.
